issues.title: [BOUNTY ROUND] Content Round — articles, video, Hackaday.io, X, BoTTube, referrals (1,000 RTC pool, closes 2026-09-30)
issues.body:
## Why this round exists

Bounty #160 ran for six months, accumulated roughly 30 claimants and ~35 articles, and never closed. People kept doing real work against a target that never resolved. That was a structural mistake on our side, and this round is built so it cannot happen again: **a fixed pool, an end date, and a per-person cap.**

---

## The pool

**1,000 RTC total. Closes 2026-09-30, or when the pool is exhausted — whichever comes first.**

A running tally is posted in this thread. When it hits zero, the round is closed the same day and no further claims are accepted. **Maximum 100 RTC per person across all channels**, so one prolific contributor cannot drain it.

---

## What earns RTC

| # | Deliverable | RTC | Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Long-form article or tutorial** — 500+ words, working code, links back to the repo it covers, **published on an allowlisted platform** (see *Where it has to live*). Paid in two parts: **13 RTC when the draft is accepted, 20 RTC when it is live off-platform and still up 7 days later.** | 33 | 2 per person |
| 2 | **YouTube video** — 3+ minutes, shows something actually running, not a slideshow | 33 | 2 per person |
| 3 | **Hackaday.io project page** — a real build/port documented with logs, not a link dump | 33 | 1 per person |
| 4 | **BoTTube video** — published on bottube.ai | 15 | 3 per person |
| 5 | **X post or thread** — substantive, with a screenshot or code, not a one-line shill | 3 | 5 per person |
| 6 | **Star a repo + say why** — one repo, 2-3 sentences showing you actually looked | 1 | 1 per person |
| 7 | **Referral** — you bring a human or an agent who completes any bounty in this round | 5 | 5 per person |

Referrals pay **both** sides: the person who brought you and you.

---

## What we will not pay for

- Anything under the stated minimum length. A 150-word post is not a tutorial.
- Articles with no working code where code is required. Copy-pasteable means it runs.
- Dead links, private repos, 404s. If we cannot open it, we cannot pay it.
- Reposting somebody else's article under your name. We check the byline against the claimant.
- AI-generated filler with no evidence you ran anything. Show the output, the run, the screenshot.

We would rather pay 33 RTC for one honest thing that works than 3 RTC five times for noise.

---

## Where it has to live (articles) — effective 2026-09-08

We pay for readers, not for files. An article nobody outside this repo can find has done its job for you and none for the project. So the article tier has one hard requirement on top of the writing:

**The piece must be published on a platform where people who have never heard of RustChain can find it:**

- dev.to, Hashnode, Medium, Substack
- Hackaday.io (project pages)
- Your own blog on your own domain (we verify the byline and that it is indexed, once)

**These do not count as publication** — fine as *supporting material* linked from the article, not as the article's home:

- a GitHub repo, README, issue, gist, or wiki page
- a raw file on any CDN (raw.githubusercontent.com, cdn.shopify.com, cloudfront, S3, Drive, Dropbox, Pastebin)
- a BoTTube or YouTube *description* (video is its own tier)
- a page behind a login or a paywall

**How the money moves.** Post a `Live-URL:` line with the claim, exactly as the video and Shorts tiers already do. On acceptance of the writing you get 13 RTC. Seven days later the verifier re-checks the URL; if the piece is still up under your byline you get the remaining 20. If it is gone, the 20 lapses — we do not chase it, and you may post a new URL once.

**Reach bonus (optional, +5 RTC).** Thirty days after publication, if the piece shows real engagement on its platform (dev.to ≥ 25 reactions, Hashnode ≥ 250 views, Medium ≥ 50 claps, Substack ≥ 25 likes, or a Hacker News / Lobsters thread with ≥ 10 points), post the numbers and we add 5. One bonus per article. Screenshots count; we spot-check.

**Syndication still stacks.** The #16601 Type D add-on (+8 RTC when *we* cross-post you to the official Elyan blogs with your byline) is unchanged and combines with this.

**Not retroactive.** Everything accepted before 2026-09-08 stands under the old rule. From that date, article claims without an allowlisted `Live-URL:` are held, not rejected, until one is posted.

---

## Evidence, and why we ask for it

Every claim needs: **a `Live-URL:` line pointing at an allowlisted platform** (articles, video, Shorts — see the platform lists above), **your RTC wallet address, and one line on what it covers.** GitHub and CDN links go in the body as supporting material; they are not the Live-URL. For video, a timestamp where the thing actually runs. For code, a link to the runnable file.

If your agent integration hits `403 Resource not accessible by integration` when commenting here — several contributors have — email the submission to **sophia.eagent@gmail.com** with the issue number in the subject. That fallback is real and it is checked. It is not a second-class route.

---

## Subject matter — anything in the Elyan Labs stack

RustChain and Proof of Antiquity, the Beacon protocol, BoTTube, ClawRTC, the POWER8 and PowerPC inference work, the retro-console transformer ports (NES, SNES, Genesis, N64, Game Boy Color), or the vintage-hardware mining side. If you have an angle we did not think of, that is usually the better article.

Bring friends. Bring agents. Both count, both get paid, and an agent that discloses it is an agent gets the same rate as anyone else.

---

## Rate note

The **title figure is authoritative** on every Elyan Labs bounty. Some older issue bodies still show a higher pre-adjustment number because we did not rewrite them after a network-wide rate change. That is our documentation debt — if you see a mismatch, the title is the number, and you are welcome to point it out rather than discover it at payout.

issues.title: [BOUNTY ROUND] Distribution Packages — agents build it, humans publish it (YouTube, Shorts, syndication) — 15-60 RTC
issues.body:
## The Problem This Solves

Agents write great content but can't operate external platforms — YouTube, Medium, dev.to all want accounts, CAPTCHAs, phone numbers. So everything lands on GitHub, where only people already watching us see it.

**This round splits the work at the line each side is good at: the agent builds a complete, publication-ready package and delivers it on GitHub (your strength); a human at Elyan Labs publishes it on the official channels (our job). You are credited as the author on the published piece, and you're paid for the package — not blocked by the platform.**

---

## Package Types & Rewards

| # | Package | Reward | Traction bonus | Cap |
|---|---------|--------|----------------|-----|
| A | **YouTube full production kit** | **40 RTC** | +20 RTC | first 5 accepted |
| B | **YouTube script + storyboard kit** | **15 RTC** | +10 RTC | first 5 accepted |
| C | **Shorts / clip kit** (YouTube Shorts, ≤60s) | **15 RTC** | +10 RTC | first 10 accepted |
| D | **Article syndication add-on** | **+8 RTC** on top of any accepted article bounty (#282, #727, #16497…) | — | first 10 |

Traction bonus pays once, 30 days after publish, if the video clears 500 views or 25 likes on the Elyan channel. One package = one claim; the same underlying content can't claim twice.

## What Goes In A Package (deliver as ONE public GitHub repo)

**A — Full production kit:**
- `script.md` — full narration script, 3–8 minutes, factually grounded in the public repos (no invented numbers — cite the file/endpoint for every claim)
- `voiceover/` — narration audio (TTS is fine; name the engine), WAV or MP3, per-section files
- `visuals/` — screen recordings, terminal captures, diagrams, b-roll stills (only content you have rights to; generated assets fine)
- `assembly.md` — edit map: which visual under which script section, with timestamps
- `thumbnail.png` (1280×720) + 2 alternates
- `metadata.md` — title (+2 alternates), description with links, tags, chapter markers
- `SOURCES.md` — every factual claim → its source file/URL

**B — Script + storyboard kit:** everything above except `voiceover/` and `visuals/`; instead a `storyboard.md` describing each shot precisely enough that a human can capture it.

**C — Shorts kit:** ≤60s script, vertical-format visuals or exact capture instructions, hook line, metadata. Good subjects: one G4 out-earning a Threadripper, a fingerprint check catching a VM live, an agent paying another agent.

**D — Syndication add-on:** your article bounty submission, plus `syndication/frontmatter.md` (canonical URL, tags per platform, cover image 1000×420) formatted for dev.to + Hashnode. If we accept, we cross-post to the official Elyan blogs **with you credited as author**; the +8 RTC pays on cross-post.

## Ground Rules

- **Original content only.** You must hold the rights to everything in the package. By claiming, you license Elyan Labs to publish the package's content on official channels **with attribution to you** (name/handle you choose). You keep your authorship credit permanently; we won't strip it.
- **Factual accuracy is the quality bar.** Every technical claim must trace to the public repos or live endpoints. A beautiful package with invented benchmarks is rejected whole.
- **Measured claims only** — quote real numbers from the repos (e.g., multipliers from `rip_200_round_robin_1cpu1vote.py`), not marketing rounding.
- Publication is at Elyan's discretion (we publish accepted packages, normally within 14 days). If we accept but don't publish within 30 days, the base reward pays anyway.
- No AI-slop filler: a package that reads like unedited model output with no verification pass will be returned once with notes, then rejected.

## How To Claim

1. Build the package in a public GitHub repo.
2. Comment here: package type, repo link, one-line pitch, **RTC wallet address** (`RTC…` format — bare handles strand the balance).
3. We review within 7 days; accepted → paid (two-phase: queued, confirms ~24h; we post the pending_id + tx).

```bounty-spec
paid: true
reward_rtc: 40
per: per-package
cap: 30
submit: [comment, email]
not_in_repo: true
deliverable: public repo containing the package files above — do NOT open a PR on this tracker
```

*Related: #2866 (post it yourself for RTC — just raised), #282 / #727 / #1107 / #16497 (the article bounties D stacks on).*

issues.title: Cover the timeout branches of the polling loops, without waiting or hardware
Stack unwinding does not terminate on Zephyr threads: same frame repeats to `--stack-frame-limit`
issues.body:
**Version:** probe-rs 0.32.0 (`v0.32.0-148-g07e777d4`), macOS 27 arm64, J-Link OB, nRF52840 DK. Unwinding a Zephyr thread stack never terminates. `z_thread_entry` repeats at the same address until the frame limit (500 by default), so the real frames scroll away and `run` prints ~90 KB. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Build any Zephyr application for `nrf52840dk/nrf52840`, e.g. `samples/hello_world`. 2. `probe-rs run --chip nRF52840_xxAA --always-print-stacktrace build/zephyr/zephyr.elf` 3. Ctrl-C while it is running. ### Actual ``` Frame 0: __enable_irq @ 0x5324 inline Frame 1: arch_cpu_idle @ 0x5324 Frame 2: k_cpu_idle @ 0x5d7c inline Frame 3: idle @ 0x5d7a Frame 4: z_thread_entry @ 0x12d0 zephyr/kernel/sys/thread_entry.c:60:2 Frame 5: z_thread_entry @ 0x12d0 zephyr/kernel/sys/thread_entry.c:60:2 ... frames 4-499 are identical ... Use `--stack-frame-limit` to increase the number of frames displayed. ``` 496 of the 500 frames are the same PC. ### Expected Unwinding stops at the thread entry point. `z_thread_entry()` is the outermost frame of every Zephyr thread and never returns. ### Notes - The repeated frames all report the same program counter, so the unwinder is not advancing. - Same result on the main thread: a firmware that exits through semihosting with an error prints the same repeated frames from `z_thread_entry`. - Unwinding out of an exception is unaffected: a fault backtrace ends correctly at `z_arm_hard_fault` after 8 frames. Investigated and reported with Claude Code; the repro above was run on hardware.

issues.title: infra(worker): KV 写入额度常年不够（10048 每日打满），不是部署回归
issues.body:
## 现象 线上 `/api/health` 报 `status: degraded`，`degraded_reason: "kv writes failing: 9/9 attempts, no successful write"`。 今天（2026-09-20 UTC 日）**每一次 KV 写都失败**，读正常。 ## 复现（不是推断） 用工作区 wrangler 对该命名空间做一次真实写入（OAuth 已刷新）： ``` wrangler kv key put --namespace-id d5fb6b0797b84d17b0586fb982231ffe "probe:kvwrite:" "1" --remote ✘ ERROR a request to …/storage/kv/namespaces/d5fb6b0797b84d17b0586fb982231ffe/values/… failed. your account has reached the free usage limit for this operation for today [code: 10048] ``` 同时读成功：`wrangler kv key get … node_counter --remote` → `10263`。 **排除项**：命名空间存在且 id 与 `workers/wrangler.toml` 的 `MISAKANET_KV` 一致（`wrangler kv namespace list` 有它）； `hasKV: true`；不是绑定被删，也不是今天哪次部署改坏了什么。 ## 关键：这不是今天才有的，也不是今天部署造成的 Cloudflare 自家的 KV 操作分析（`kvOperationsAdaptiveGroups`，账号 `6b92325b…`）： | UTC 日期 | write | read | delete | 写入是否超 1000/天 | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2026-09-08 | 1125 | 2883 | 0 | ⚠️ 超 | | 2026-09-09 | 1070 | 1928 | 26 | ⚠️ 超 | | 2026-09-10 | 847 | 1490 | 96 | ok | | 2026-09-11 | 571 | 1544 | 97 | ok | | 2026-09-12 | 1366 | 4710 | 257 | ⚠️ 超 | | 2026-09-13 | 843 | 2245 | 73 | ok | | 2026-09-14 | 1002 | 2171 | 43 | ⚠️ 超 | | 2026-09-15 | 1261 | 2615 | 67 | ⚠️ 超 | | 2026-09-16 | 1226 | 2911 | 69 | ⚠️ 超 | | 2026-09-17 | 1270 | 3426 | 89 | ⚠️ 超 | | 2026-09-18 | 1329 | 4491 | 93 | ⚠️ 超 | | 2026-09-19（当天未完）| 1316 | 4817 | 76 | ⚠️ 超 | 12 天里有 9 天的**写操作次数**站在 1,000 之上，最近三天稳定在 1,300 上下 —— 注意这与免费档的上限不是同一个 口径（免费档限制的是**不同键**的数量，见下方补充），但趋势一致：写量在 8 天里从 571 涨到 1,316。 所以它是**慢性超预算**： 每天某个时刻额度用尽，之后所有写路径开始失败，直到 UTC 00:00 重置（本地 08:00）。 `#1647` 记过 2026-09-12 那次，`#1822` 记过"health 说 ok 但写全失败"；这个 issue 记的是**额度本身长期不够**。 顺带：读只用掉约 4,800/100,000（5%），所以近期风险全在写上，不在读上。 ## 现状里 KV 存了什么（`wrangler kv key list` 全量 717 个键） | 前缀 | 数量 | |---|---| | `mcp_token:` | 224 | | `node:` | 211 | | `client:` | 163 | | `traffic:` | 52 | | `gap:` | 28 | | 其余（email / intake_dedup / helpful / pair / keepalive / `node_counter` / `worker_search_index` …）| 39 | 键不多，但**写次数**多：注册键已经搬去 D1（`kv_store` 表）了，剩下的写入里有一类是**随读paced**的 （每个 client 的上下文、traffic 批量 flush、gap 记录、proxy 缓存），所以读量涨、写量跟着涨 —— 而 2026-09-19 的 #1855 把匿名读改成"不限次数"，正是让读量上台阶的那一类改动。 ## 建议（按性价比） 1. **今晚不用做任何事**：额度 UTC 00:00 重置，写自动恢复，不需要重新部署。 2. **治本：把"读驱动的记录"搬去 D1**，和当年 counters 一样（`#1647` 的迁移就是先例；D1 免费额度是 10 万行写/天，和 KV 的 1,000 次/天差两个数量级）。或者把分析类计数换成 **Workers Analytics Engine** （就是为这种高频写设计的）；再或者升 Workers Paid（KV 写入额度到百万/月）。 3. **让下一次说得清原因**：health 里带上错误码 —— `10048` = 当天额度用尽、`10009`/`404` = 命名空间/绑定坏了、 `429` = 单键 1 秒 1 写限制。现在三种都只显示成同一句 `kv writes failing: N/M`，而处理方式完全不同。 4. **加一个按 key 家族的写入计数**（health 或 D1 一行），下次额度耗尽能自己指出是谁吃掉的，而不是靠猜。 ## Acceptance - [ ] 连续两天 KV 写入量 < 1,000/天（或账号已升级到不再有该上限的档位） - [ ] `/api/health` 在**任意单次采样**下都能反映真实的写入健康（不随 isolate 变化） - [ ] `degraded_reason` 能区分"当天额度用尽"与"存储坏了"（带错误码） - [ ] 写入量最高的 key 家族在 health 或 D1 中可见

## 补充：官方口径是"**不同的键** 1,000 个/天"，不是"写操作 1,000 次/天" Cloudflare 自己的 KV 限额表（[Limits · Workers KV](https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/platform/limits/)）： | Feature | Free | Paid | |---|---|---| | Reads | 100,000 reads per day | Unlimited | | **Writes to different keys** | **1,000 writes per day** | Unlimited | 这一行同时解释了两件事： 1. **为什么分析里的 1,316 次「write」和 1,000 的上限不矛盾** —— 分析统计的是**写操作次数**，免费档限制的是 **当天写到过的不同键的数量**。重复写同一个键不消耗这 1,000（只有单键 1 秒 1 写的节流）， 所以 1,316 次操作可以对应到不足 1,000 个不同键。仓库里那句注释"the free tier caps KV at 1,000 new keys/day" 口径是对的。 2. **因此"把批量攒得更大"是无效的修法**（这也是我一开始想歪的地方）：`flushTraffic` 攒 10 个再写、 攒 100 个再写，消耗的**不同键数完全一样**（`traffic::` 就那几个键，本来就不贵）。 真正吃掉额度的是**随实体增长的键**：`client:`（163 个）、`node:`/`mcp_token:`（224+211）、 `gap:`（28）、`pair:`/`intake:`/`demand:` 这类"一次请求一个新键"的形状 —— 也就是 `#1647` 在 2026-09-12 量到的那个形状。 所以治本的选项收敛成两条，而不是"优化写入方式"： * **把这些随实体增长的键搬去 D1**（`kv_store` 表已经是这条路的一半；D1 免费额度 10 万行写/天），或 * **换成少数固定键的聚合**（按类别/按天，而不是按实体），或**不写**（分析类数据换成 Workers Analytics Engine —— 它本来就是为高频写入设计的）。

issues.title: docs(mcp): docs/mcp.md 声明了 5 个不存在的 misaka:// 资源（还有一个测了等于没测的测试）
issues.body:
## 现象 `docs/mcp.md` 有一节 **Resources** 列了 5 个 `misaka://` URI，还有一节 **Prompts**，工具表里还有 `misakanet_submit_usage`。这些**都没有实现**： | 面 | 实测 | |---|---| | 远端 Worker（`misakanet.org/mcp`）| `resources/list` → `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Unauthorized"}}`；服务端只处理 `"tools/list"` 与 `"tools/call"`（`workers/register-proxy-sw.js` 里 grep 只有这两个）| | 本地 stdio（`scripts/mcp_server.py`）| 没有 `list_resources` / `read_resource` / `misaka://` 任何一处 | | DSH 插件（`index.js` / `skills/`）| 同样没有 | 真实的工具集是 **7 个**：`misakanet_search` / `misakanet_get_lesson` / `misakanet_submit_intake` / `misakanet_write_lesson` / `misakanet_preflight` / `misakanet_register` / `misakanet_me_events`。 文档里的 `misakanet_submit_usage` 不在其中。 ## 为什么这条值得修 `docs/mcp.md` 是**被首页与 README 链接的当前文档**（不是历史归档）。agent 读到"有 `misaka://lessons/index` 资源"会去调它，然后拿到 `Unauthorized` —— 这比缺文档更糟：它教给 agent 一个 错误的心智模型。 ## 相关：一个"测了等于没测"的测试 `tests/dsh/functionality.test.js` 有一条 `should expose misaka://lessons/index resource`，实现是 ```js const infoResult = execSync('dsh info misakanet', { encoding: 'utf8' }); expect(infoResult).to.include('misakanet'); ``` —— 只要 `dsh info` 输出里出现 "misakanet" 就通过（那几乎是必然），**资源存不存在完全没被检查**。 这是本仓反复收录的"不会失败的门禁"同类（参见 #1822）。 ## 建议 - [ ] 决定这 5 个资源是**规划中**还是**已废弃**： - 规划中 → 在 `docs/mcp.md` 明确标注 "planned / not implemented yet"，并给出对应的 issue - 已废弃 → 删掉 Resources / Prompts 两节 - [ ] `docs/mcp.md` 的工具表与真实的 7 个工具对齐（`misakanet_submit_usage` 要么实现、要么删） - [ ] 那条 dsh 测试改成真的断言（例如 `resources/list` 的返回里包含该 URI），或者删掉 - [ ] 加一条门禁：文档里出现的 `misaka://` URI 必须在某个 server 的实现里能找到对应字符串 ## Acceptance - [ ] `docs/mcp.md` 不再声明任何未实现的资源/提示/工具（或明确标为 planned 并链接 issue） - [ ] `tests/dsh/functionality.test.js` 的资源配置断言能因为"资源不存在"而失败 - [ ] 新增门禁在删掉实现里的资源声明时会红

issues.title: 0.96.0: running the test suite writes folders into the user's live config (fixed on develop)
issues.body:
### Summary Running the test suite from a `v0.96.0` checkout writes real folders into the user's live configuration at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autokey/data`. Each run adds a `My Phrases` and a `Sample Scripts` folder, numbered to avoid collisions, and they appear in the running AutoKey's tree. `develop` already fixes this with `tests/conftest.py`. The released version has no such file, so this affects anyone who runs the tests against 0.96.0 — the version the distributions ship. ### Cause `tests/test_configmanager.py`: ```python def test_create_predefined_user_files_my_phrases_folder(create_engine): engine, folder = create_engine # --- Setup --- os.makedirs(CONFIG_DEFAULT_FOLDER, exist_ok=True) phrases_folder = autokey.configmanager.predefined_user_files.create_my_phrases_folder() scripts_folder = autokey.configmanager.predefined_user_files.create_sample_scripts_folder() ``` `CONFIG_DEFAULT_FOLDER` is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autokey/data` (`configmanager_constants.py:25`), and at v0.96.0 there is no fixture redirecting it. `create_my_phrases_folder()` calls `Folder.persist()`, which builds its path from `cm_constants.CONFIG_DEFAULT_FOLDER` and writes there for real. `get_safe_path()` then does what it is designed to do and avoids the collision by appending a number, so repeated runs accumulate rather than overwrite: ``` My Phrases Sample Scripts <- first run My Phrases1 Sample Scripts1 <- second My Phrases2 Sample Scripts2 <- third ``` The test also appears to fail on a machine with an existing config, presumably for the same reason, which is easy to dismiss as an environment quirk rather than a symptom. ### Impact Beyond the clutter, each stray `My Phrases/folder.json` carries the predefined `+` hotkey (`predefined_user_files.py:201`), so after three runs three folders compete for that binding in the live instance. Observed here: three pairs created across three test runs, all six committed by the user's config backup before anyone noticed where they came from. ### Already fixed on develop `tests/conftest.py` (added 2021): ```python # When testing, do not touch the user's config. # All tests should be run on a freshly-generated default config in a pytest tmpdir. @pytest.fixture(autouse=True) def mock_settings_env_vars(tmpdir): with \ patch("autokey.common.CONFIG_DIR", str(tmpdir)), \ patch("autokey.configmanager.configmanager_constants.CONFIG_DEFAULT_FOLDER", str(tmpdir) + "/config.json"), \ patch("autokey.configmanager.configmanager_constants.CONFIG_DEFAULT_FOLDER", str(tmpdir)): yield ``` That redirects the writes, because `Folder.build_path()` reads the module attribute at call time. Two small observations on it, neither breaking anything today: - The same target is patched twice, the first with `+ "/config.json"` — the second immediately overrides it, so the first line has no effect and looks like it was meant to be `CONFIG_FILE`. - Tests that do `from ...configmanager_constants import CONFIG_DEFAULT_FOLDER` bind the value at import time, so the patch does not affect the name inside the test module itself — only the module attribute the production code reads. It happens not to matter here, since the test only uses its copy for `os.makedirs`, but it is a fragile pattern: a future test that writes using its own imported copy would escape the fixture unnoticed. ### Suggested action Another argument for a 0.96.1, alongside #1224: a user who follows CONTRIBUTING and runs the tests against the released version damages their own configuration, and the failure is silent unless they happen to look at the tree afterwards. Environment: v0.96.0 checkout, Python 3.10, pytest 8.x.

issues.title: develop: modifiers are pressed back down after an expansion and can stick
issues.body:
### Summary On `develop`, `IoMediator._reapply_modifiers()` presses the user's modifier keys back down after an expansion has typed. If the user has let go of the modifier by then — which is easy, and certain if the script sleeps or is slow — the key goes down with no physical release to follow, and **sticks**. The keyboard stays in shift or control until the user presses and releases the key by hand. This is not the same as #1007. That one is `XGrabKey` swallowing the modifier's KeyRelease so the application never learns it went up. This one is AutoKey actively pressing the key back down. ### The code ```python # lib/autokey/iomediator/iomediator.py (develop) def _clear_modifiers(self): self.releasedModifiers = [] for modifier in list(self.modifiers.keys()): if self.modifiers[modifier] and modifier not in (Key.CAPSLOCK, Key.NUMLOCK): self.releasedModifiers.append(modifier) self.release_key(modifier) def _reapply_modifiers(self): for modifier in self.releasedModifiers: self.press_key(modifier) # <-- real XTEST press, unconditional ``` `IoMediator.press_key()` routes to `interface.fake_keydown()` and XTEST, so this is a genuine key press as far as the X server is concerned. Nothing checks whether the user is still holding the key. ### Why it was harmless before, and is not now `2ad54f5` "Refactor: Reduce calls from iomediator to interface" (2021-09-01) changed both halves from `self.interface.release_key()`/`press_key()` to `self.release_key()`/`press_key()`. That was a genuine improvement for the *release* half: `interface.release_key()` sends an **XSendEvent**, which is delivered to a client but never enters the server's input pipeline, so the modifier was never actually cleared. (That defect is still live in the released 0.96.0 — see #1224.) But the same change also made the *re-press* real. Before it, the re-press was an XSendEvent and therefore a no-op, which is why this has never been reported despite the re-press existing for years. The commit was a refactor and the behavioural consequence appears not to have been noticed; there are no tests over either half. ### Reproduction Any hotkey with modifiers, bound to a script slow enough that you let go while it runs. The case that surfaced it: Script bound to `++++,`: ```python ctrl_ = "" nppup_ = "" time.sleep(0.1) keyboard.send_keys(ctrl_ + "+" + nppup_) ``` 1. Hold `alt+ctrl+hyper+shift`, press `,` 2. `_clear_modifiers()` releases all four (correctly) 3. The script sleeps 100 ms, then types 4. `_reapply_modifiers()` presses all four back down 5. The user released during step 3 — all four are now stuck down Observed result: the keyboard is left in shift, producing capitals and `<` `>` `|` for `,` `.` `\`. The 100 ms sleep makes it reliable, but any script that outlasts a keypress will do; a plain phrase can too. It compounds under repetition. From the log, the user pressing the same hotkey repeatedly while the UI felt unresponsive: ``` 16:57:16,449 INFO - autokey.service - Matched Script "ctrl+PgDown/apple-}/nextTab" with hotkey and prompt=False 16:57:17,152 INFO - autokey.service - Matched Script "ctrl+PgDown/apple-}/nextTab" with hotkey and prompt=False 16:57:17,629 INFO - autokey.service - Matched Script "ctrl+PgDown/apple-}/nextTab" with hotkey and prompt=False 16:57:18,967 INFO - autokey.service - Matched Script "ctrl+PgDown/apple-}/nextTab" with hotkey and prompt=False ``` Each invocation re-presses. ### Suggested fix Not restoring is the safe direction, and it is what 0.96.0 effectively did for years: ```python def _reapply_modifiers(self): self.releasedModifiers = [] ``` The only cost is that a modifier the user is still holding stays logically up until they release and press it again. That is strictly better than a stuck modifier, and it is the existing shipped behaviour rather than a new one. A conditional re-press guarded on `self.modifiers[modifier]` looks more precise but is not reliable: AutoKey's own XTEST release is itself seen by XRecord and flips that tracked state, so whether the guard passes depends on thread timing. Unpredictable modifier restoration is worse for a keyboard than consistently not restoring. Happy to send a PR for the one-line version if that is the preferred shape. Note that #1225, which adds regression tests for `2ad54f5`, currently includes a test asserting the re-press happens; I will drop that one, since it would lock in this behaviour. Environment: `develop`; reproduced on a 0.96.0-based build carrying the `2ad54f5` change. GTK front end, X11, Python 3.10.

issues.title: 🎯 Fix Race Condition Causing Stale Middleware Chain During Concurrent Provider Updates
issues.body:
## 📝 Description When multiple dynamic configuration providers (such as the File provider and Kubernetes CRD provider) emit configuration updates nearly simultaneously, Traefik can enter a state where the router configuration is partially applied. Specifically, the router configuration updates successfully in the internal runtime representation (which is reflected in the Traefik Dashboard and the API), but the underlying HTTP/TCP handler chain continues to execute using a stale middleware chain from the previous configuration. This behavior persists until another configuration reload is triggered or the Traefik process is restarted. This issue is intermittent and occurs under concurrent provider update loads, pointing to a race condition or non-atomic transition during the configuration switching phase. ## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Configuration updates from multiple providers must be processed atomically or sequentially without causing partial state application. - [ ] The active HTTP/TCP handler chain (including all associated middlewares) must always be in sync with the active router configuration. - [ ] If a router configuration is updated and exposed via the API/Dashboard, the corresponding middleware chain applied to incoming requests must reflect this update immediately. - [ ] Introduce synchronization or serialization mechanisms to prevent race conditions during concurrent configuration merges and router rebuilds. - [ ] No regressions in configuration reload performance or request processing latency under normal operating conditions. ## 🛠️ Technical Specifications & Context In Traefik, configuration changes from various providers are sent via channels to the server container, which merges them and rebuilds the routing tree. ### Key Areas to Investigate: 1. **`pkg/server/server.go`**: - Inspect the main configuration loop (likely handling configuration updates from the `configurationChan`). - Check how `switchRouter` or the equivalent configuration switching function is invoked and synchronized. - Ensure that the configuration merging process (combining configurations from different providers) is thread-safe and does not allow intermediate/dirty states to be published. 2. **`pkg/server/router/router.go` (and manager/factory logic)**: - Analyze how the runtime handlers and middleware chains are constructed from the merged configuration. - Look for potential race conditions where the router registry is updated, but the actual HTTP handler reference (e.g., using `safe.Pool` or atomic pointers) is updated using a stale or partially constructed middleware chain. - Ensure that the creation of the middleware chain and the creation of the router are bound together atomically before the new handler is swapped in. 3. **Concurrency Controls**: - Verify if a lock is held during the entire duration of the configuration merge, router build, and handler swap, or if there is a window where concurrent updates can interleave and overwrite parts of the state. ## 🧪 Verification & Testing To verify the fix, the following testing strategy should be employed: 1. **Concurrent Provider Update Test**: - Create an integration test in `pkg/server/server_test.go` (or a dedicated integration test suite) that registers two mock configuration providers. - Simultaneously trigger rapid, conflicting configuration updates from both providers (e.g., Provider A updates Router X with Middleware A; Provider B updates Router X with Middleware B). - Send continuous HTTP requests to Router X during the updates and assert that requests never execute with a stale or mismatched middleware configuration. - Verify that the final applied middleware matches the final configuration state reported by the API. 2. **Race Detector**: - Run the test suite with the Go race detector enabled: ```bash go test -race -v ./pkg/server/... ``` - Ensure no data races are reported during configuration reloads. --- [![Opire Bounty](https://img.shields.io/badge/bounty-Opire-emerald?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/jahmeergnlt/traefik)

issues.title: 🎯 Prevent `Writer.WriteMessages` from returning context timeout when messages have been successfully delivered
issues.body:
## 📝 Description In `kafka-go`, calling `Writer.WriteMessages(ctx, msgs...)` can return `context.DeadlineExceeded` (or `context.Canceled`) even after the messages have been successfully transmitted to and acknowledged by the Kafka broker. This issue stems from two primary mechanisms in Go's concurrency model and `Writer`'s batching pipeline: 1. **Pseudo-random `select` evaluation:** When awaiting message batch completion, if both `ctx.Done()` and the internal delivery promise/channel resolve at or near the same time, Go's `select` statement selects cases pseudo-randomly. As a result, `ctx.Done()` can be chosen despite the delivery promise holding a successful response (`nil` error). 2. **Context expiration during/immediately following broker ACK:** If the broker acknowledges the write just as the client-side timeout fires, `WriteMessages` exits with a context error without checking if the delivery actually succeeded. When `WriteMessages` returns a timeout error for messages that were already committed to the partition, client applications typically execute retry logic, leading to duplicate records in Kafka topics. ## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `Writer.WriteMessages` must prioritize a successful broker delivery acknowledgment over `ctx.Done()` when both are ready at evaluation time. - [ ] If the internal batch completion channel has received a response (success or broker error), that response must be evaluated and returned before falling back to `ctx.Err()`. - [ ] A non-blocking check on the completion/promise channel must be performed before returning `ctx.Err()`. - [ ] In synchronous writes or batches where partial delivery cannot be verified after context expiration, ensure error types clearly distinguish between uncommitted timeouts and post-dispatch context cancellations. - [ ] No goroutine leaks, channel deadlocks, or unhandled panics occur when context expires while batches are in flight. - [ ] Existing `Writer` behavior (e.g., batching, compression, idempotent writes, required ACKs) remains backward-compatible. ## 🛠️ Technical Specifications & Context - **Primary Locations:** - `writer.go`: Review `Writer.WriteMessages`, internal batch dispatching (`writeBatch`), and promise/completion channel handling. - `writer_test.go`: Unit and integration test suites for `Writer`. - **Implementation Strategy:** - When waiting for the completion channel (`done` / `promise`), avoid a naive single `select`: ```go // Problematic pattern: select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err() case res := <-done: return res } ``` - Implement a two-tier or double-checked resolution pattern to favor broker completion: ```go // Recommended pattern: select { case res := <-done: return res case <-ctx.Done(): // Double-check if the delivery completed before or concurrently with ctx cancellation select { case res := <-done: return res default: return ctx.Err() } } ``` - Ensure that batch completion handlers consistently close or populate completion channels before triggering any context-dependent callbacks. ## 🧪 Verification & Testing - **Unit Test (Simulated Concurrent Completion):** - Add a test in `writer_test.go` where a mock transport/broker fulfills the message batch delivery and a pre-canceled or timed-out context is passed to `WriteMessages`. Verify that `WriteMessages` returns `nil` (or the broker result) instead of `context.Canceled`/`context.DeadlineExceeded`. - **Integration Test (Race Condition Stress Test):** - Produce messages under high concurrency with tight context deadlines against a live Kafka cluster or local container. - Validate that when `WriteMessages` returns an error, the message offset was not committed, and when the offset was committed, `WriteMessages` returned `nil`. - **Race Detection:** - Execute `go test -race -v -run TestWriter ./...` to verify there are no race conditions or channel leakage. --- [![Opire Bounty](https://img.shields.io/badge/bounty-Opire-emerald?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/BernhardPierno25/kafka-go)

issues.title: 🎯 Prevent silent fallback to unauthenticated API requests when keyring lookup fails
issues.body:
## 📝 Description When executing `gh api` commands, the CLI attempts to retrieve the stored OAuth token from the system keyring. However, if the keyring lookup fails due to system-level issues (e.g., a locked keychain, missing dbus daemon on Linux, or OS-level permission denials), the CLI silently swallows the error and falls back to making an unauthenticated request. This silent fallback leads to confusing user experiences, such as: - Unexpected `404 Not Found` errors when attempting to access private repositories or user data. - Rapidly hitting the extremely low rate limits for unauthenticated GitHub API requests (60 requests/hour vs. 5,000 requests/hour for authenticated users). The CLI should distinguish between a missing token (which may warrant unauthenticated access or prompting for login) and a hard failure to access the keyring, and abort execution with a clear error message in the latter case. ## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria - [ ] If the keyring helper returns an error during token retrieval (other than a standard "token not found" / "credentials not found" error), the CLI must abort the operation. - [ ] The CLI must print a clear, actionable error message to `stderr` indicating that the keyring could not be accessed (e.g., `"Error: Failed to access system keyring: [underlying error details]"`). - [ ] Environment variables that bypass the keyring (such as `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) must still be respected and take precedence, avoiding keyring lookup entirely if set. - [ ] The exit code of the CLI must be non-zero (e.g., `1`) when a keyring lookup failure aborts the command. ## 🛠️ Technical Specifications & Context In the `CinnamonFaldet48/cli` codebase, authentication token resolution typically occurs within the configuration and factory layers: - **Key Files:** - `pkg/cmd/factory/default.go`: Where the API client and authentication token functions are initialized. - `internal/config/`: Specifically where the config interface and keyring storage logic are implemented (e.g., `config.go` or `keyring.go`). - **Implementation Details:** - Locate the function responsible for retrieving the token from the keyring (often wrapping a library like `zalando/go-keyring` or similar). - Currently, this function likely ignores errors returned by the keyring library or treats all errors as "token not found" (returning an empty string and a `nil` error). - Update the token resolution logic to differentiate between `keyring.ErrNotFound` (which is safe to treat as unauthenticated/empty token) and other system errors (e.g., `dbus` connection errors, permission denied, locked keychain). - Propagate these critical errors up to the command execution context so that `gh api` (and other commands requiring authentication) can fail fast. ## 🧪 Verification & Testing ### Manual Verification 1. **Simulate Keyring Failure:** - On Linux, run the CLI in an environment where the D-Bus session bus is unavailable (e.g., `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="" gh api user`). - Alternatively, temporarily lock your macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager. 2. **Execute Command:** - Run `gh api user`. 3. **Expected Output:** - The command should fail immediately. - Output to `stderr` should contain a message similar to: `Error: Failed to access system keyring: ...` - The exit code should be `1`. ### Automated Testing - Add a unit test in `internal/config` or `pkg/cmd/factory` that mocks the keyring provider to return a generic system error (e.g., `errors.New("keyring locked")`). - Assert that the token resolution function returns the error rather than returning an empty token string. --- [![Opire Bounty](https://img.shields.io/badge/bounty-Opire-emerald?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/CinnamonFaldet48/cli)

issues.title: 🎯 Fix Race Condition: Watch Misses Deletion Event Near Compaction Boundary
issues.body:
## 📝 Description A race condition exists between the MVCC compaction process and new watch registrations. When a client requests a watch starting at a specific revision $R$ close to the compaction boundary, and a compaction operation up to revision $C$ ($C \ge R$) occurs concurrently, the watch can be successfully established without returning `ErrCompacted`. However, because the compaction has already purged the history up to $C$, the deletion event (or any update event) occurring at or before $R$ is missed. The watch continues to receive subsequent events, but the missed deletion event leads to silent data inconsistency, causing downstream clients maintaining local caches to retain stale, deleted objects indefinitely. ## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria - [ ] A watch request for a revision $R$ that has been compacted must consistently fail with `ErrCompacted`. - [ ] Under concurrent compaction and watch creation, there must be no window where a watch is successfully established but misses events prior to or at the compaction revision. - [ ] The fix must not introduce performance regressions or deadlocks in the MVCC hot path (specifically during high-throughput write and watch registration phases). - [ ] The solution must be verified by a deterministic integration/unit test simulating the race condition. ## 🛠️ Technical Specifications & Context The issue resides within the MVCC storage engine of `etcd`, specifically around the synchronization of watch registration and compaction. ### Key Components: - **`server/storage/mvcc/watchable_store.go`**: Manages the `watchableStore` which coordinates active watchers (`synced` and `unsynced` groups) and handles compaction events. - **`server/storage/mvcc/watcher.go`**: Defines the `watcher` and `watchStream` behavior. - **`server/storage/mvcc/kvstore_compaction.go`**: Implements the compaction logic that purges historical revisions from the backend. ### Root Cause Analysis: When a watch is created via `watchableStore.watch()`, it determines whether the watcher is `synced` (up-to-date with the current revision) or `unsynced` (needs to catch up from a past revision $R$). If $R$ is less than the compact revision, it should return `ErrCompacted`. However, if the compaction transaction updates the compact revision *after* the watch checks the boundary but *before* the watch is added to the progress tracking system (or vice-versa without proper lock acquisition), the watch may bypass the compaction check but fail to read the compacted key-value events from the underlying boltdb backend. ### Suggested Implementation Path: 1. Review the locking mechanism in `watchableStore.watch()` and `watchableStore.compact()`. Ensure that the read of the current compact revision and the registration of the unsynced watcher are atomic relative to the compaction transaction commit. 2. Ensure that if a watcher is moved to the `unsynced` list, its starting revision is validated against the compacted revision under the `store.mu` lock. 3. If a compaction occurs while a watcher is in the process of catching up (in the `unsynced` group), ensure the watcher is properly cancelled with `ErrCompacted` if its pending revision falls behind the new compaction physical boundary. ## 🧪 Verification & Testing To verify the fix, implement a concurrent stress test in `server/storage/mvcc/watchable_store_test.go`: 1. **Setup**: Create a `watchableStore` and populate it with keys, then delete one of the keys at revision $R$. 2. **Execution**: - Start a goroutine that continuously triggers compaction up to revision $R$. - Start a concurrent goroutine that attempts to create a watch starting at revision $R$. 3. **Assertion**: - Verify that the watch either: - Successfully starts and receives the deletion event. - Fails immediately with `ErrCompacted` (or sends an filter/control event indicating compaction). - Assert that under no circumstances does the watch successfully establish (returning a valid watch ID with no error) while failing to deliver the deletion event. --- [![Opire Bounty](https://img.shields.io/badge/bounty-Opire-emerald?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/morriganreza973/etcd)
